Header: 2027-05-04 15:00 PT — Duration approx 56m. Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ava (CTO, SummitOps), Liam (Head of Platform), Sophie (ML Eng), Noah (Product), Ivy (Security).

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our SE. Marcus might drop in late. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Ava (SummitOps CTO): Doing well, thanks. We wanted to make this concrete — we have an internal timeline to decide by end of May whether we run a pilot.
[00:18] Jordan: Great, that's super helpful. High level today we want to align on success criteria, what you want to measure in the benchmark, how to integrate (SDK vs OpenAI-compatible endpoints), and the mechanics of tool/function calling plus structured output.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll go into some of the benchmark details and a proposed script. But first, Sophie — can you give a short snapshot of your workload? QPS, typical prompt lengths, and any special tooling requirements?
[00:40] Sophie (ML Eng): Sure. So we have two primary flows: a conversational helper embedded in our Ops dashboard and a batch enrichment job. Dashboard traffic is spiky — 80% bursts around 100 to 400 qps for short prompts, median tokens ~50, p95 token length about 220. The enrichment jobs are lower qps but longer context — average doc size 1.2k tokens, some up to 6k. We are also using a small toolchain for internal lookups — basically a function-call pattern to hit our inventory API and secure vault.
[01:10] Liam (Head of Platform): To add — we need audit logs for every request and response, and we have strict data residency for EU customers, can't leave EU for those requests.
[01:20] Jordan: Perfect, that frames the constraints. On the integration side, we support our native SDKs (Python/Node/Go) and also OpenAI-compatible endpoints. For most customers the OpenAI-compatible path is the fastest lift because you can swap endpoints; our SDK adds helpers for batching, prefix caching, and structured output validation.
[01:35] Ava: We are considering both. Product team likes the quick swap with OpenAI-style endpoints, but Platform likes the richer controls with the SDK. What's the risk with using OpenAI-compatible endpoints?
[01:45] Priya: Tradeoffs are around feature parity — the OpenAI-compatible API maps to most generation and chat flows, and function-calling works, but some runtime optimizations like automatic prefix/KV cache tuning and advanced batching knobs are only surfaced in our SDK. Also, SDK exposes easier tracing hooks for the Console.
[02:05] Sophie: For the function-calling bit — we need strict JSON output from the model so downstream parsers don't break. How do you handle structured output enforcement?
[02:13] Priya: Two layers — model-side: we recommend a strict schema with a validator step. Redwood Optimize can run an eval set against candidate models to measure schema compliance. Runtime-side: our SDK has a structured-output helper that validates and optionally repairs outputs, and we stream a validation score. For OpenAI-compatible flows we provide a schema validator library you can plug in.
[02:35] Noah (Product): Can the SDK do automated fallback — e.g., if the model returns invalid JSON, fall back to a more robust model or re-run with a repair prompt?
[02:42] Priya: Yes, you can define fallback policies. We also support automatic retries with a different quantization profile or lower-latency model if cost/latency thresholds are breached. Those are easier to orchestrate via the SDK but can be implemented over the OpenAI endpoints with additional logic on your side.
[03:05] Ava: Ok, about benchmarks — what do you need from us to run something meaningful?
[03:10] Jordan: We propose a two-phase benchmark: 1) Synthetic microbench for latency/throughput to verify p50/p95 under a controlled QPS curve; 2) Replay benchmark using your real traces with token distribution to measure cost per million tokens, avg latency, model correctness on structured outputs, and schema compliance rates.
[03:28] Priya: For microbench, we'll need expected QPS spikes, concurrency (number of parallel connections), and target latency SLOs. For replay, the 7-day request traces Sophie mentioned plus a labelled set of 1k prompts for correctness eval. We'll provide a sample script that runs both locally and against Redwood hosted endpoints.
[03:47] Sophie: We can share traces but they contain PII in some payloads — is there a redaction step you recommend?
[03:54] Priya: Yes, we recommend removing or tokenizing PII. We can accept a synthetic anonymized trace if you prefer. If this goes to a private deployment, you can also run benchmarks in your VPC so data never leaves your network.
[04:10] Ivy (Security): We need to confirm SOC2 scope and whether we can get test-level audit logs for the pilot. Also KMS integration: can Redwood integrate with our keys?
[04:19] Jordan: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and we have an enterprise plan that brings that to Dedicated. For hosted customers, we offer encrypted-at-rest and in-transit plus audit logs; customer-managed keys require Private or a dedicated contract. We'll send the SOC2 report and security pack after this call.
[04:36] Liam: Data residency — EU traffic must be served in the eu-west region. Is that supported for both hosted and dedicated?
[04:43] Priya: Yes, we have region pinning. Hosted EU region is available for a production pilot; for strict residency plus audit controls and KMS you might prefer Private in your VPC or a Dedicated reservation deployed into EU nodes. We'll show the tradeoffs in the pilot plan.
[05:00] Noah: Success criteria — what should we list so procurement and execs can sign off?
[05:05] Jordan: From our side a typical success criteria set for this POC: 1) Latency SLO: p95 below X ms for dashboard flows (we'll map X to your SLO, e.g., 700ms), 2) Schema compliance >= 98% on structured output eval, 3) Cost estimate within target threshold (e.g., under $Y per 100k requests), 4) Integration effort <= 4 engineer-weeks to get to pilot, and 5) Security/compliance checks passed — SOC2, audit logging, and KMS gating if needed.
[05:40] Ava: That aligns. For us, product cares about schema compliance and latency during peak bursts. Platform cares more about steady-state cost and operational observability. Security will block if KMS can't be used for EU data.
[05:56] Priya: We'll parameterize the plan so you can pick SLOs and cost targets; the benchmark will give empirical numbers.
[06:05] Jordan: Timeline-wise — you need a go/no-go end of May. Proposed schedule: artifact handoff (traces + schema) by May 6, benchmark script + pilot SOW by May 7, scheduling benchmark windows May 12-14, run benchmarks and share results May 15-17, review + decide May 20-21. Does that fit?
[06:26] Liam: Tight but doable if Sophie gets the traces out this week.
[06:31] Sophie: I can get the 7-day traces and 1k prompt labels to you by May 6. I'll redact PII before upload.
[06:39] Ivy: We'll confirm data residency constraints and internal compliance contacts by May 8.
[06:45] Jordan: Great. Now a couple of specific technical items for Priya to cover — caching, batching, and kv cache behavior for long contexts.
[06:53] Priya: Sure. For long-context workloads like your enrichment jobs, we recommend a split approach: a streaming ingestion to prefill KV cache and a chunked generation lane. Our runtime supports KV cache reuse across related requests and prefix caching which reduces repeated token computation. For very long contexts (4k+), we recommend the quantized model variants and tuned kernel selection to keep latency predictable.
[07:18] Sophie: Are you providing quantized variants of the models, or do we bring our own?
[07:22] Priya: We host quantized variants for the models in our catalog and can recommend profiles based on your workload. If you have a licensed model you want to bring, the runtime can load it but the quantization path will need an onboarding step.
[07:36] Noah: On the SDK vs OpenAI endpoint again — if we go OpenAI-compatible are we losing telemetry we need for observability?
[07:42] Jordan: OpenAI-compatible endpoints still yield request/response logs and basic metrics in the Console, but the SDK is richer: token-level cost breakdowns, built-in tracing hooks, ability to attach route-level rollouts, and direct callstack maps. It also makes canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks simpler.
[08:00] Ava: For the benchmark we want p50/p95 latency, throughput at different concurrency ramps, cost per million tokens, and schema compliance. Anything else?
[08:08] Priya: We'll add parse-correctness (percentage of outputs that parse as valid JSON), a schema-field accuracy metric (for key fields), and resource usage for Dedicated — GPU utilization at various batch sizes.
[08:20] Priya: Also, we'll include a small noise test for adversarial prompts that purposely break JSON to test your parsers and our repair heuristics.
[08:29] Sophie: Helpful. Regarding tool-calling — we plan to use the model to emit calls like {"action":"lookup_ticket","ticket_id":1234}. We need guaranteed exactly one call per request when it's expected. How do you guarantee idempotency and exactly-once semantics?
[08:42] Priya: Practically, at the model layer you can't enforce exactly-once, but our SDK offers call verification and a lightweight transaction pattern: the SDK tags calls with idempotency tokens and a short TTL. On receipt, your API can check the token to dedupe. For hosted flows you'll need to implement or use our library for dedupe. For Dedicated/Private we can help with hook integrations.
[09:05] Liam: Token cost — can we get a ballpark how cost scales with longer contexts in your hosted service?
[09:11] Jordan: Ballpark: cost scales linearly with input+output tokens. But we can reduce billable tokens with prefix caching and KV reuse; in some workloads we've seen token cost drop 20-40% after caching. We'll estimate for your traces during the replay benchmark.
[09:27] Ivy: What about encryption KMS — you mentioned customer-managed keys for Private. If we do hosted, can we still get exportable audit logs for our legal team?
[09:36] Jordan: Yes, hosted provides audit logs with retention options. Export to your SIEM is supported. For access to raw decrypted content tied to keys, that's only with Private / customer-managed keys.
[09:48] Sophie: A couple of nitty-gritty items — do you support function_call name matching vs schema-only? We have a router that expects a name field.
[09:56] Priya: We support both. With the OpenAI-compatible model calling you can use function names; SDK exposes a richer contract mapping so you can map model outputs to typed function signatures.
[10:07] Noah: Any blockers for running the replay benchmark in our environment (VPC) vs hosted?
[10:13] Priya: If you want the replay inside your VPC we can provide a Private pilot package and an installer. That takes a bit more ops coordination (network peering, KMS, and a small deployment window). Hosted is faster to start but you must sanitize traces.
[10:28] Ava: For procurement — pricing tiers for pilot vs production?
[10:32] Jordan: We'll include pilot pricing (time-limited credits plus a small infra reservation) and production estimates for both hosted and Dedicated. The SOW will show a delta for Dedicated reserved capacity.
[10:40] Liam: We'll need an estimate on engineering effort to integrate the SDK vs just swapping endpoints — helps justify the cost.
[10:45] Jordan: We'll add an integration effort estimate, broken down into SDK integration (approx 2-4 engineer-weeks depending on complexity), OpenAI-compatible swap (1-2 engineer-weeks), and an additional week for testing and rollout. We'll put that in the pilot plan.
[11:01] Priya: Quick note on rollout strategies — we recommend a canary of 5-10% traffic, observe schema compliance and latency, then step to 25% and 50% before full cutover. The SDK supports automated rollouts and fallback policies; with the OpenAI endpoints you'll need to orchestrate these steps.
[11:20] Noah: That works. Any regulatory flags for EU customers we should call out?
[11:24] Ivy: For us it's mainly GDPR logging, data subject access requests, and ensuring encryption keys remain in-region. We'll share a short compliance checklist.
[11:31] Jordan: We'll add that to the security pack.
[11:34] Priya: Last technical note — for batch enrichment with long contexts we recommend an async pipeline that stores KV-cache keys and reuses them across related records; that reduces repeated decoding and cuts cost. We'll include an example pattern in the benchmark docs.
[11:49] Sophie: Sounds good. Who will lead the benchmark run on Redwood side?
[11:53] Jordan: Priya will lead the benchmark setup and Marcus will help with infra if needed. I'll coordinate the pilot SOW and commercial terms.
[12:01] Ava: Ok to recap — Sophie provides traces by May 6, Jordan/Priya deliver pilot plan and benchmark script by May 7 and 10 respectively, schedule a 2-hour benchmark window May 12-14, and we reconvene after results to decide.
[12:15] Jordan: That's right. Anything else we missed?
[12:18] Liam: Maybe just one more on monitoring — can we stream logs to our Datadog account?
[12:22] Priya: Yes, we support Datadog, Splunk, and other sinks. We'll include config snippets.
[12:29] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll look out for the docs and the SOW.
[12:33] Jordan: Thank you. We'll follow up with the pilot plan and security pack. Linking artifacts in the follow-up: pilot-plan.docx (internal link), security-pack.pdf (link), benchmark-script.yaml (example).
[12:48] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and truncated words — this is an AI-generated meeting transcript with medium accuracy.
